# Guideline 2 - Your character is yours You are free to create and play whatever characters you like, and to portray them however you want. All we ask is that your character stays believable while you are playing them.
- Play as many characters as you like, and change, reinvent or retire them whenever you want. - Personality, quirks, mood and outlook are entirely up to you, and they can grow over time. - Within a round, keep your character coherent. A sudden change of heart is fine when there is an in-character reason for it, not just a mechanical advantage. - Carrying the same character across rounds and developing them is encouraged, but never required. - Your character remembers the shifts they survived, so let that history show: old friends, old rivals, lessons learned. See [textlink="Guideline 5" link="GuidelineG5"] for exactly what carries over.
Part of that freedom is getting into trouble. If your character is the type to start a fight in the hallway, go for it, but be ready to face the consequences in character and to [textlink="build that conflict through roleplay" link="GuidelineG3"].
